title: Signal-driven Task Composer for Admin Utilities
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: operators frequently run ad-hoc sequences of small remedial steps (probe, collect, restart, scale, rotate keys). These sequences are often manual, duplicated across SREs, and brittle when signals change. We need a way to author, synthesize, and safely execute short remediation flows from telemetry signals without shipping full runbooks or creating custom playbooks per incident.
proposed_solution:
Build a Signal-driven Task Composer (SDTC): a server-side composer that transforms structured signals (alerts, anomaly scores, trace markers, console events) into parameterized 'tasklets' that can be executed as safe, auditable admin actions. Key features:
- Tasklet library: idempotent micro-ops (check, collect, restart, promote, set-quota, backoff) implemented as composable primitives.
- Signal mapping rules: JSON/YAML rules that map signal attributes to tasklet templates and parameter extraction.
- Dry-run & validation: simulate effects against a sandbox state, validate permissions and preconditions.
- Safety fences: RBAC gates, rate limits, human confirmation hooks, and automatic rollback steps.
- Execution engine: orchestrates tasklets with retries, concurrency control, KV checkpointing, and structured telemetry.
- Audit & provenance: immutable action records linked to the originating signal, integrated with audit logs and the Console trace view.
- Extensibility: SDK hooks for adding new primitives and custom validators by platform teams.
technical_approach: Implementation will be phased: 1) design tasklet schema and serializer (YAML first, JSON later), 2) implement a shim that composes tasklets into an execution graph, 3) integrate a sandbox toggle that pipes dry-runs into the existing ops-sandbox harness, 4) add a signal-rule editor in Console for SREs, and 5) rollout safe defaults and a small pilot group. The runtime will reuse existing operator agentlet executor for idempotent primitives and the admin-proxy for permissioned actions. Task definitions will carry a policy fingerprint to fast-fail incompatible nodes at runtime.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Adding another orchestration layer increases operational surface area; mitigate by reusing agentlet runtime and existing monitoring dashboards.
- Incorrect signal mapping can trigger noisy actions; mitigate by shipping conservative default mappings, progressive rollout, and analytics on false positives.
- Security risk for automated privileged actions; require mandatory approval for high-impact tasklets and KMS-protected parameters.
- Requires SRE culture change; plan training and runbook migration docs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDTC can convert at least three distinct alert types into tasklet graphs and run them in dry-run mode with no side effects.
2) Execution engine records structured audit logs and links back to originating signal ID in Console.
3) Safety fences (RBAC gate + rate limit) block a high-impact tasklet in >95% of simulated abusive scenarios.
4) Pilot team (Platform SRE) executes 10 production dry-runs and approves promotion to live execution.
5) Documentation and a short tutorial exist in Confluence and Console help.
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal alpha for Platform SREs (2 weeks) — only dry-run and audit recording enabled. Phase B: limited live exec with manual approvals (4 weeks) — scoped to staging clusters. Phase C: broader pilot with automated low-risk primitives (4 weeks). Phase D: global default with config flags and monitoring alerts (2 weeks). During each phase we'll collect false-positive metrics, operator feedback, and safety incidents.
metrics: - number_of_dry_runs, number_of_live_executions, false_positive_rate_by_signal, mean_time_saved_per_incident, safety_gate_block_rate, audit_events_per_run
